Avengers: Endgame :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
The film was announced in October 2014 as *Avengers: Infinity War – Part 2*, but Marvel Studios later removed this title. The Russo brothers joined as directors in April 2015, with Markus and McFeely signing on to write the script a month later. It is a conclusion to the story of the MCU up to that point, ending several main characters' story arcs. The plot revisits moments from earlier films, bringing back actors and settings from throughout the franchise. Filming began in August 2017 at [Pinewood Atlanta Studios](/wiki/Pinewood_Atlanta_Studios "Pinewood Atlanta Studios") in [Fayette County, Georgia](/wiki/Fayette_County,_Georgia "Fayette County, Georgia"), shooting [back-to-back](/wiki/Back-to-back_film_production "Back-to-back film production") with *Infinity War*, and ended in January 2018. Additional filming took place in the [Metro](/wiki/Metro_Atlanta "Metro Atlanta") and [downtown Atlanta](/wiki/Downtown_Atlanta "Downtown Atlanta") areas, [New York state](/wiki/New_York_state "New York state"), [Scotland](/wiki/Scotland "Scotland"), and [England](/wiki/England "England"). The official title was announced in December 2018. With an estimated budget range of $356–400 million, *Endgame* is one of the [most expensive films](/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_films "List of most expensive films") ever produced.

*Avengers: Endgame* premiered at the [Los Angeles Convention Center](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Convention_Center "Los Angeles Convention Center") on April 22, 2019, and was released in the United States on April 26 as part of [Phase Three](/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe:_Phase_Three "Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase Three") of the MCU. The film received positive reviews from critics, with praise for its direction, acting, musical score, action scenes, visual effects, and emotional weight, with critics lauding its culmination of the 22-film story. 1. **[^](#cite_ref-12)** 
   Saint-Exupéry was born at No. 8 rue Peyrat, later rue Alphonse Fochier, and still later rue Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, in [Lyon's 2nd arrondissement](/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Lyon "Arrondissements of Lyon").[[9]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWebster199412-9) He was the third of five children (and nicknamed 'Tonio'), his older sisters were Marie-Madeleine ("Biche", 26 January 1897 – 1927), Simone ("Monot", 26 January 1898 – 1978), and his younger siblings François (1902–1917) and Gabrielle ("Didi", 1903–1986). His parents were Viscount Jean de Saint-Exupéry (1863–1904; different sources name his father as Jean-Marc or Caesar de Saint-Exupéry[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECommire1980154-11)) and Viscountess Marie, née Boyer de Fonscolombe (1875–1972). He was baptized in a Catholic ceremony in his great-aunt's chapel on 15 August 1900 in [Saint-Maurice-de-Rémens](/wiki/Saint-Maurice-de-R%C3%A9mens "Saint-Maurice-de-Rémens"); his godfather was his uncle, [Roger de Saint-Exupéry](/w/index.php?title=Roger_de_Saint-Exup%C3%A9ry&action=edit&redlink=1 "Roger de Saint-Exupéry (page does not exist)"), [Earl of Miremont](/w/index.php?title=Earl_of_Miremont&action=edit&redlink=1 "Earl of Miremont (page does not exist)") (1865 – August 1914, killed leading his battalion in Maissin, Belgium, during the First World War), his godmother was his aunt Madeleine Fonscolombe.[[10]](#cite_note-SaintExCom2-10)

fanoutqa_009623.t: QS World University Rankings :: History :: chunk_0001
fanoutqa_009623.x:
QS World University Rankings :: History :: chunk_0001
QS was founded by Nunzio Quacquarelli in 1990 to provide information and advice to students looking to study abroad. Since then, the company expanded to include a wider range of higher education-focused products and services before partnering with *THE* in 2004 to create the *THE*–QS World University Rankings.

A perceived need for an international ranking of universities was highlighted in December 2003 in [Richard Lambert](/wiki/Richard_Lambert "Richard Lambert")'s review of university-industry collaboration in [Great Britain](/wiki/Great_Britain "Great Britain")[[13]](#cite_note-13) for [HM Treasury](/wiki/HM_Treasury "HM Treasury"), the finance ministry of the United Kingdom. Amongst its recommendations were world university rankings, which Lambert said would help the UK gauge the global standing of its universities. Between 2004 and 2009, QS produced the rankings in partnership with *THE*. In 2009, *THE* announced they would produce their own rankings, the *[Times Higher Education World University Rankings](/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings "Times Higher Education World University Rankings")*, in partnership with [Thomson Reuters](/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters"). *THE* cited an asserted weakness in the methodology of the original rankings,[[14]](#cite_note-14) as well as a perceived favoritism in the existing methodology for science over the humanities,[[15]](#cite_note-15) as two of the key reasons for the decision to split with QS. *THE* created a new methodology with Thomson Reuters, and published the first *Times Higher Education World University Rankings* in September 2010.

QS publishes the rankings results in the world's media and has entered into partnerships with a number of outlets, including *[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* in the United Kingdom and *[Chosun Ilbo](/wiki/Chosun_Ilbo "Chosun Ilbo")* in [South Korea](/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"). Shiba Inu :: Appearance :: chunk_0001
The breed's standard colors are red, sesame, black sesame, red sesame (sashige), black and tan, or cream. All have a cream to white ventral color, known as *urajiro* (裏白). *Urajiro* literally translates to "underside white".[[3]](#cite_note-AKCstandard-3) The *urajiro* is required in the following areas on all coat colors: on the sides of the muzzle, on the cheeks, inside the ears, on the underjaw and upper throat, inside of legs, on the abdomen, around the vent and the ventral side of the tail. On reds: commonly on the throat, fore chest, and chest. On blacks and sesames: commonly as a triangular mark on both sides of the fore chest.[[6]](#cite_note-urajiro-6)

Other than the *urajiro* areas, the cream color is considered a "major fault" by both the [Japan Kennel Club](/wiki/Japan_Kennel_Club "Japan Kennel Club") and [American Kennel Club](/wiki/American_Kennel_Club "American Kennel Club").[[7]](#cite_note-JKCStandard-7) It is not intentionally bred in a show dog, as the required markings are not discernible. However, a cream coat is acceptable according to [The Kennel Club](/wiki/The_Kennel_Club "The Kennel Club") (UK) breed standard.[[8]](#cite_note-KCstandard-8)

Shiba Inu have a double coat; the topcoat is stiff with guard hairs and the undercoat is soft and plush.[[9]](#cite_note-PetMD-9) Although less common, Shiba Inu can also be long-haired as a result of inheriting the recessive gene from both parents.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

Haroche was born in [Casablanca, Morocco](/wiki/Casablanca "Casablanca"), to Albert Haroche (1920–1998), from a [Moroccan Jewish](/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Morocco "History of the Jews in Morocco") family, and Valentine Haroche, born [Roubleva](/wiki/Rublev_(surname) "Rublev (surname)") (1921–1998), a teacher who was born in [Odessa](/wiki/Odessa "Odessa") to a Jewish family of physicians who relocated to [Morocco](/wiki/Morocco "Morocco") in the early 1920s. His family had mixed [Sephardic](/wiki/Sephardic_Jews "Sephardic Jews") and [Ashkenazi](/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jews "Ashkenazi Jews") origins.[[6]](#cite_note-6) His father, a lawyer trained in [Rabat](/wiki/Rabat "Rabat"), was one of seven children born to a family of teachers, Isaac and Esther Haroche, who worked at the [*École de l’Alliance israélite*](/wiki/Alliance_Isra%C3%A9lite_Universelle "Alliance Israélite Universelle") (AIU).[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11)[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13)

Both paternal grandparents of Serge Haroche had been AIU students in their respective hometowns of [Marrakesh](/wiki/Marrakesh "Marrakesh") and [Tétouan](/wiki/T%C3%A9touan "Tétouan") (the school which Esther Azerad attended in Tétouan had been founded in 1862; it was the first school of the AIU network).[[14]](#cite_note-14)

Haroche's family left Morocco in 1956 at the end of the [French protectorate](/wiki/French_protectorate_of_Morocco "French protectorate of Morocco") treaty, and settled in France.

Main article: [Frankford Yellow Jackets](/wiki/Frankford_Yellow_Jackets "Frankford Yellow Jackets")

The [Frankford Athletic Association](/wiki/Frankford_Yellow_Jackets "Frankford Yellow Jackets") was organized in May 1899 in the parlor of the Suburban Club. The cost of purchasing a share in the association was $10. However, there also were contributing memberships, ranging from $1 to $2.50, made available to the general public. The Association was a community-based non-profit organization of local residents and businesses. In keeping with its charter, which stated that "all profits shall be donated to charity", all of the team's excess income was donated to local charitable institutions. The original Frankford Athletic Association apparently disbanded prior to the 1909 football season. Several of the original players from the 1899 football team kept the team together, and they became known as Loyola Athletic Club. In keeping with Yellow Jackets tradition, they carried the "Frankford" name again in 1912, to become the Frankford Athletic Association.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

In the early 1920s, the Frankford Athletic Association's Yellow Jackets gained a reputation as being one of the best independent football teams in the nation. In 1922, Frankford absorbed the Philadelphia City Champion team, the Union Quakers of Philadelphia. That year, Frankford captured the unofficial championship of Philadelphia. During the 1922 and 1923 seasons, the Yellow Jackets compiled a 6–2–1 record against teams from the National Football League. This led to the Association being granted an NFL franchise in 1924, thus becoming the [Frankford Yellow Jackets](/wiki/Frankford_Yellow_Jackets "Frankford Yellow Jackets"). In spite of winning the NFL championship in 1926, midway through the [1931 season](/wiki/1931_NFL_season "1931 NFL season"), the Yellow Jackets went bankrupt and were forced to cease operations.[[13]

The **cosmetic industry** describes the industry that manufactures and distributes cosmetic products. These include colour cosmetics, like foundation and mascara, skincare such as moisturisers and cleansers, haircare such as shampoos, conditioners and hair colours, and toiletries such as bubble bath and soap. The manufacturing segment of the industry is dominated by a small number of [multinational corporations](/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation") that originated in the early 20th century, but the distribution and sale of cosmetics is spread among a wide range of different businesses. Cosmetics must be safe when customers use them in accordance with the label's instructions or in the conventional or expected manner. One measure a producer may take to guarantee the safety of a cosmetic product is product testing. FDA occasionally does testing as part of its research program or when looking into potential safety issues with a product. Both the cosmetics business and consumers can benefit from the FDA's resources on product testing.

The largest cosmetic companies are [L'Oreal](/wiki/L%27Oreal "L'Oreal"), [Estée Lauder](/wiki/The_Est%C3%A9e_Lauder_Companies "The Estée Lauder Companies"), [Coty](/wiki/Coty "Coty"), [Nivea](/wiki/Nivea "Nivea"), [Shiseido](/wiki/Shiseido "Shiseido") and [Chanel](/wiki/Chanel "Chanel").[[1]](#cite_note-1) The [market volume](/wiki/Market_volume "Market volume") of the cosmetics industry in Europe and the United States is about EUR €70 billion per year,
